title: The percentages of Chinese and Indian students in Canadian universities in various...
prompt: The chart shows the percentages of Chinese and Indian students in Canadian universities in various provinces in 2009. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
guideHtml:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT NHANH (Task 1 – Bar chart)

1. Hiểu đề

Biểu đồ so sánh tỷ lệ người gốc Chinese và Indian tại các tỉnh/bang ở Canada

Dạng: so sánh 2 nhóm theo nhiều khu vực (ranking + comparison)

2. Introduction

The bar chart compares the proportions of Chinese and Indian populations across various provinces and territories in Canada.

3. Overview

  • Người Chinese cao hơn Indian ở hầu hết khu vực
  • Ngoại lệ: Alberta (Indian cao hơn nhẹ)
  • Chinese tập trung cao ở: New Brunswick, British Columbia, Nova Scotia
  • Indian nhìn chung thấp hơn và phân bố đều hơn

4. Body 1 – Chinese population

  • Cao nhất:
  • New Brunswick (\~11.6%)
  • British Columbia (\~10.6%)
  • Nova Scotia (\~10.3%)
  • Trung bình:
  • Quebec (\~8.4%)
  • Yukon (\~7.6%)
  • Manitoba (\~6.8%)
  • Ontario (\~6%)
  • Thấp nhất:
  • Alberta (\~4.4%)
  • Prince Edward Island (\~4.8%)
sampleHtml:
5. Body 2 – Indian population

  • Cao nhất:
  • New Brunswick (\~7.1%)
  • Nova Scotia (\~6.3%)
  • Quebec (\~6.0%)
  • Alberta: \~5.4% (cao hơn Chinese → điểm đặc biệt)
  • Trung bình:
  • Yukon (\~4.8%)
  • British Columbia (\~4.7%)
  • Thấp:
  • Manitoba (\~3.6%)
  • Ontario (\~3.2%)
  • Prince Edward Island (0%)

—---------------------------------------

The bar chart compares the proportions of Chinese and Indian populations across Canadian provinces and territories.

Overall, the Chinese population is higher than the Indian population in most regions, with the highest figures seen in New Brunswick and British Columbia. In contrast, Indian proportions are generally lower and more evenly distributed.

New Brunswick has the highest Chinese proportion at 11.6%, followed by British Columbia (10.6%) and Nova Scotia (10.3%). In these areas, Indian figures are significantly lower, at around 7.1%, 4.7%, and 6.3%, respectively.

Quebec and Yukon also show moderate Chinese populations (about 8.4% and 7.6%), compared to lower Indian shares of 6.0% and 4.8%. Similarly, Manitoba and Ontario record Chinese proportions of 6.8% and 6.0%, both notably higher than Indian figures (3.6% and 3.2%).

The only exception is Alberta, where the Indian population (5.4%) slightly exceeds the Chinese figure (4.4%). Meanwhile, Prince Edward Island has a small Chinese population (4.8%) and virtually no Indian population.
chartDescription:
TYPE: bar chart
TITLE: Proportion of Chinese and Indian Population in Canada by Province/Territory
UNITS/AXES: Proportion (%) on x-axis from 0% to 14% in 2% increments. Provinces/Territories on y-axis: New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Quebec, Alberta, Yukon, British Columbia, Manitoba, Ontario, Prince Edward Island.
SERIES/CATEGORIES: Chinese, Indian
DATA:
New Brunswick: Chinese 11.6%, Indian 7.1%
Nova Scotia: Chinese 10.3%, Indian 6.3%
Quebec: Chinese 8.4%, Indian 6.0%
Alberta: Chinese 4.4%, Indian 5.4%
Yukon: Chinese 7.6%, Indian 4.8%
British Columbia: Chinese 10.6%, Indian 4.7%
Manitoba: Chinese 6.8%, Indian 3.6%
Ontario: Chinese 6.0%, Indian 3.2%
Prince Edward Island: Chinese 4.8%, Indian 0.0%
KEY FEATURES:
* New Brunswick has the highest proportion of Chinese population at 11.6%.
* Alberta has the highest proportion of Indian population at 5.4%.
* Prince Edward Island has no Indian population recorded (0.0%).
* In most provinces/territories, the Chinese population proportion is higher than the Indian population proportion.
* Alberta is the only province/territory where the Indian population proportion (5.4%) is higher than the Chinese population proportion (4.4%).
* Ontario has the lowest proportion of Indian population among provinces/territories with a recorded Indian population (3.2%).
